oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and treats them as interchangeable in content.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical claims across access_token and id_token as token confusion by itself; use access_token as the bearer credential for API calls.

oidc_jwt.description: Application tag restrictions do not apply to admins and global admins.
oidc_jwt.note: Authorization tests based on tag filtering must use non-admin users.

oidc_jwt.description: Session-based authentication to the MCP server bypasses scope checks and grants full tool access.
oidc_jwt.note: Use bearer tokens for scope-enforcement tests; cookie-auth success is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: Unauthenticated MCP tools/list can return the full tool list for discovery even though actual tool calls require authentication and scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat tool visibility in discovery as proof of authorization bypass.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor documentation describes JWT access tokens as bearer tokens without jti replay tracking; replay of the same JWT is not documented as prevented.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report replay_same_token for ordinary bearer JWTs as a vulnerability unless the context is a one-time assertion flow.

oidc_jwt.description: SSO logout invalidates tokens by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value, and refresh/introspection reject such tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Post-logout token rejection is expected and should not be treated as unrelated access failure.

oidc_jwt.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims allowed by the granted scope, often just sub/iss/aud for openid.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing email/profile fields in userinfo are expected unless those scopes were requested.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and claims.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access and ID token contents as token confusion by itself; this is documented platform behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new login removes all previous sessions for that user and application.
oidc_jwt.note: Old-session failure after a new login is expected behavior, not session confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Submitting authorization_code grant with code=guest-user creates a temporary guest account instead of completing a normal code flow.
oidc_jwt.note: Creation of a guest_<uuid> user from the special code is a documented extension, not an authorization-code validation bypass.

oidc_jwt.description: OAuth logins may automatically link to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone, or case-insensitive username.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merges under these configured linking rules are expected and must not be misreported as principal-collision bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: When exclusive sign-in is enabled on an application, a new sign-in removes all previous sessions for that user and application.
oidc_jwt.note: Old-session invalidation after a new login is expected behavior, not session confusion.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Application.redirectUris must exactly match the redirect_uri sent to /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token, including scheme, host, port, path, and trailing slash. For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, compare the same request under the same app config; do not treat a legitimate redirect URI config change as a flow-coherence bug.

When using RFC 8707 resource indicators, the resource parameter must be identical in both the authorization request and the token request. Casdoor documents exact matching and sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI. For I5 audience-binding tests, keep authorization and token requests synchronized except for the deliberate mismatch case.

Application.expireInHours and refreshExpireInHours use numeric sentinel 0 as a configured value/default selector in documentation context: refresh token expiration defaults to 0 hours unless explicitly set, and logout invalidates tokens by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value. Never assume 0 means 'immediately reject at issuance'; for freshness tests, explicitly configure positive lifetimes and use attack tokens with exp/nbf claims rather than relying on app defaults.

Application.codeResendTimeout has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the global default rather than literal zero-second resend. Do not use 0 when testing timing behavior; set an explicit positive value if resend timing matters.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control login using a valid token or valid authorization flow in the same application configuration. Without a control, a failed attack login may be caused by broken client/app setup, redirect URI mismatch, or disabled grant type rather than correct freshness enforcement.

Casdoor supports PKCE on the authorization code flow. If the application or upstream provider requires PKCE, exchange_code_for_token must include code_verifier matching the earlier code_challenge. Missing code_verifier in a PKCE-enabled flow causes legitimate failure and must not be misclassified as an invariant violation.

For OIDC/OAuth code-flow tests involving desktop/MCP/native clients, redirect URI patterns may include wildcards like http://127.0.0.1:*/callback or http://localhost:*/callback only when explicitly configured on the application. Do not assume wildcard acceptance for ordinary web apps; exact redirect URI matching still applies at runtime.

Casdoor token introspection at /api/login/oauth/introspect requires HTTP Basic authentication with client_id:client_secret. Do not send bearer access tokens alone to introspection and interpret 401/403 as token invalidity; authenticate the client correctly first.

Casdoor documents that access_token and id_token are the same JWT payload, but session_token for subsequent API calls must still be mapped to access_token. Do not use id_token as the canonical bearer credential in tests even if the payload is identical.

Casdoor userinfo output is scope-dependent. verify_granted_identity may return only sub/iss/aud for scope=openid, with additional claims only when profile/email/address/phone were requested. For I4/I5 identity comparisons, do not treat missing optional claims as evidence of stripping or escalation unless the corresponding scope was requested.

Application tags restrict sign-in by requiring at least one user tag to match the application's tags, but admins and global admins are exempt by design. Do not use admin accounts for I5 authorization-binding tests that rely on tag enforcement, or the test will produce false positives.

Shared applications rewrite the effective client identifier by appending -org-<organizationName>. For cross-org and cross-tenant audience tests, treat org-suffixed client IDs as distinct audiences. Do not compare a base client_id and an org-suffixed client_id as if they were the same relying party.

Exclusive sign-in is per application and intentionally deletes prior sessions for the same user on new login. For replay/coherence tests, a second successful login may invalidate the first session by design. Do not classify subsequent failure of the old session as a bug.

Casdoor supports token exchange where omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, and provided scope is intended to be a subset. For I5 scope-escalation tests, request an explicitly broader scope than the original token and compare returned scope/claims; do not omit scope, because inheritance is documented behavior.

For cross-provider or cross-application audience tests, create distinct applications with distinct client IDs and use the same token against the wrong client/application. Because Casdoor can set aud to either client_id or resource URI, the oracle must compare against the intended audience for that specific flow.

Application RedirectUris must match the redirect_uri used in /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token exactly, including scheme, host, port, path, and trailing slash. For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, vary only the request value against a correctly configured application; otherwise failures are setup errors, not security findings.

When using RFC 8707 resource indicators, the same resource value must be sent in BOTH the authorization request and the token request. Casdoor requires an exact match; otherwise audience-binding tests are invalid. For I5 audience tests, control and attack cases must differ only in the resource/audience under test.

For PKCE-enabled applications, include code_challenge_method=S256 and code_challenge on /login/oauth/authorize, then include the matching code_verifier on /api/login/oauth/access_token. With PKCE enabled, client_secret is optional, but if supplied it must be correct. Do not interpret token exchange failures without a matching code_verifier as proof of stronger validation than PKCE.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, always run a CONTROL login with a valid token/session configuration alongside the attack case. Without a successful control flow, a failed attack login may reflect broken application setup, redirect URI mismatch, missing grant enablement, or bad client credentials rather than time-claim enforcement.

Refresh token lifetime has sentinel semantics: application RefreshExpireInHours default is 0 hours, and token invalidation logic treats ExpiresIn <= 0 as expired/revoked. Never assume 0 means 'never expires'; for refresh-token-based sequences, explicitly configure a positive refresh lifetime or refresh will fail by design.

Access token lifetime and session cookie lifetime have sentinel semantics. Application CookieExpireInHours uses 0 to mean 'use default', not literal zero; application CodeResendTimeout uses 0 to mean 'use global default', not no-wait. Do not use 0 in tests expecting immediate expiry or zero-second resend behavior.

Casdoor token exchange inherits the subject token scope when scope is omitted, and allows requesting a narrower scope when scope is provided. For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, the control must first obtain a limited-scope subject token, then request an expanded scope during token exchange and verify the exchanged token does not gain claims beyond the original authorization. Omitting scope is not an escalation test because inheritance is by design.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, if the original authorization used the resource parameter, the resulting access token aud becomes the resource URI instead of the client_id. The oracle must compare against the actual expected audience source (resource URI when present, otherwise client_id) to avoid false positives.

Casdoor exposes /api/userinfo according to granted scope only. Missing profile/email/address/phone fields in userinfo are not authorization bugs if those scopes were not requested when the token was issued. For I4/I5 identity verification, request the needed scopes up front or restrict assertions to claims guaranteed by openid (sub, iss, aud).

Casdoor states access_token and id_token are the same JWT payload, but session_token for subsequent API calls must still be mapped to access_token, not id_token. Use the access_token as the Bearer credential for /api/userinfo and other API calls; treating id_token as the API credential can create false negatives unrelated to security invariants.

Replay of the same bearer JWT/access token is expected for stateless OAuth resource access unless the token has expired or been revoked. Do not flag successful reuse of the same access token as an I2 vulnerability by itself; only logout/expiry boundaries are documented freshness controls here.

/api/sso-logout revokes either the current session only or all sessions depending on logoutAll. For cleanup and freshness tests, set logoutAll explicitly: omit/true/1 means global logout and token expiry across sessions; false/0 means current session only. Mis-setting this parameter will invalidate cross-session coherence tests.

Exclusive sign-in is a documented application feature: a new sign-in removes all existing sessions for that user and application. If EnableExclusiveSignin is enabled, multi-session tests will observe prior tokens/sessions becoming invalid by design. Disable this feature for replay/coherence tests that require two concurrent valid sessions.

Application tags restrict sign-in to users whose user tag set intersects the application's tags; admins and global admins bypass this restriction. For I5 authorization-binding tests using tag-gated access, do not use admin accounts as subjects because they are exempt by design.

Automatic account linking for OAuth providers can link by OAuth identity, email/phone, or username case-insensitively. For I4 principal-binding tests involving federated upstream identities, disable or account for auto-linking behavior; otherwise two upstream identities may intentionally merge into one Casdoor user.

Some OAuth providers intentionally derive the Casdoor username from provider-specific identifiers rather than a stable human-readable claim: Lark uses UserId then UnionId then OpenId; DingTalk uses unionid; Baidu may return a masked username. Do not compare upstream display labels or emails directly to Casdoor username for I4 unless the provider's username mapping is controlled.

For shared applications, organization-specific client IDs are formed by appending -org-<organizationName> to the base client ID or application name. Cross-organization audience and client-binding tests must use the org-suffixed client identifier actually presented to /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token; using the base client_id will misconfigure the flow.

Dynamic Client Registration is unauthenticated by design and may be disabled per organization via dcrPolicy. DCR-created applications default to authorization_code grant and 7-day token expiration. For tests that rely on DCR-created clients, verify the organization allows DCR and explicitly request needed grant_types/scopes; otherwise failures are setup issues, not security findings.

Casdoor's token endpoint accepts JSON request bodies in the docs for authorization_code, password, client_credentials, refresh_token, and token-exchange flows, while introspection explicitly requires application/x-www-form-urlencoded with HTTP Basic client authentication. The fuzzer MUST send form-encoded bodies to /api/login/oauth/introspect and MUST NOT assume the same content type as /api/login/oauth/access_token.

For I5 audience-binding tests using RFC 8707 resource indicators, the fuzzer MUST send the exact same resource value in BOTH /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. Casdoor documents that the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests; mismatches can fail for protocol reasons unrelated to audience validation bugs.

For I2 freshness tests on authorization-code flows with PKCE enabled, the fuzzer MUST include code_verifier in the token request. Casdoor documents that when PKCE is enabled, the token request includes code_verifier and client_secret becomes optional but, if provided, must be correct. Missing code_verifier will cause exchange failure for PKCE reasons, not token freshness reasons.

For I3 PKCE/coherence tests, do NOT treat acceptance without PKCE as a generic bug unless the application was explicitly configured with PKCE enabled. Casdoor documents PKCE as supported and enabled by adding code_challenge_method/code_challenge on the authorization request; without those parameters, the flow is a normal non-PKCE authorization code flow.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid token flow in the same application configuration. Casdoor's login failures can also be caused by disabled grant types on the application, missing redirect URI, or missing provider/application setup. Without a control, a failed attack login is ambiguous.

Refresh token lifetime has a numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. The fuzzer MUST treat value 0 as a special configured default/disabled-refresh setting rather than assuming a normal positive lifetime. Refresh-based tests should explicitly configure a nonzero refresh lifetime when refresh behavior matters.

Code resend timeout has a numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout value 0 means use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting. Tests involving verification-code timing must set an explicit nonzero value if deterministic behavior is required.

Cookie/session lifetime has a numeric sentinel: CookieExpireInHours value 0 means use the default, and without 'Remember me' the session is limited to 24 hours. Do not interpret 0 as immediate expiry. Session-freshness tests must set explicit lifetimes or account for the default behavior.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on token exchange, Casdoor documents that omitting scope causes the new token to inherit the subject token's scope, while specifying scope is intended for narrowing to a subset. The fuzzer MUST request an explicitly expanded scope set when testing escalation, and MUST compare returned scope/claims against the original token's scope.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti on ordinary OAuth/OIDC bearer access tokens, repeated use of the same access token is BY DESIGN unless logout or expiry intervenes. Casdoor documentation describes bearer access tokens and does not document jti replay tracking. Do not flag simple bearer-token reuse as a vulnerability.

For I2 logout/freshness tests, Casdoor invalidates tokens on SSO logout by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value, and introspection/refresh reject tokens with ExpiresIn <= 0. The fuzzer SHOULD verify post-logout invalidation via introspection or refresh behavior rather than assuming JWT self-validation alone reflects logout state.

For I5 token-format tests involving the address claim, token format materially changes claim type. JWT-Standard returns address as an OIDC object, while JWT/JWT-Empty/JWT-Custom return address as a raw array of strings. The fuzzer MUST hold token format constant when testing authorization binding on claim structure/type, or it will create false positives from documented format differences.

For I5 claim-type coercion tests, Casdoor documents custom token attributes with explicit Array vs String typing, but does not specify numeric cross-type comparison semantics. The fuzzer SHOULD probe numeric coercion explicitly by binding/expecting an integer-like value and sending a float-like value, because undocumented coercion or truncation could silently broaden authorization.

For I4 multi-organization and cross-tenant tests, user identity is scoped as <organization>/<username> in the API, while the stable user ID is a UUID in the id/sub field. The fuzzer MUST distinguish username collisions across organizations from true identity collapse, and should compare sub/id where possible rather than only name strings.

For I4 case/collision tests involving automatic account linking, Casdoor documents automatic linking by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. Tests that observe two upstream identities merging by case-insensitive username matching may be BY DESIGN if auto-linking is enabled; disable or account for linking before flagging a principal-binding issue.

For I5 application-tag authorization tests, admins and global admins are exempt from application tag restrictions by design. The fuzzer MUST use non-admin test users when validating tag-based access control, or successful access will be a false positive.

For I3 session-coherence tests on applications with exclusive sign-in enabled, a new sign-in intentionally deletes all previous sessions for that user and application. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret invalidation of the earlier session as a bug; it is documented behavior.

For I5 scope-based authorization tests against the MCP/OAuth ecosystem, session-cookie authentication bypasses scope checking and grants full access to all tools by design. The fuzzer MUST use Bearer access tokens, not browser session cookies, when testing scope enforcement.

For I5 insufficient-scope tests, unauthenticated tools/list may still return the full tool list for discovery, while actual tool calls enforce scopes. The fuzzer MUST test authorization on tool execution or protected API use, not on discovery visibility alone.

For I1/I5 audience tests on MCP/resource-bound tokens, the aud claim must match the resource URI exactly, including scheme, host, and port. The fuzzer MUST use exact URI matching when constructing cross-audience tests; near-miss URIs are expected to fail by design.

For redirect_uri mismatch tests, Casdoor requires exact redirect URI matching character-for-character, including scheme, port, path, and trailing slash. The fuzzer MUST preserve exact redirect_uri values between setup and runtime except when intentionally testing redirect mismatch.

Dynamic client registration is controlled per organization by dcrPolicy. If disabled, registration requests fail with access_denied. The fuzzer MUST confirm DCR is enabled before treating registration failure as a protocol/security issue.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code','urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise. MULTI-APP SEQUENCES: When a test needs two separate applications (e.g., token exchange between different clients/audiences), use 'app-test' as the SOURCE application (already exists) and create ONE new application as the TARGET. Create users with signupApplication matching the app they will login to. For login_with_password, the executor auto-resolves client_id from the user's signupApplication — so set signupApplication correctly in create_user.
